tags.chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

question.text: When the first electron gain enthalpy <math> <mrow> <mrow><mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mi>Δ</mi><msub> <mi>H</mi> <mrow> <mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow> </msub> </mrow> <mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow> </math> of oxygen is <math><mo>-</mo><mn>141</mn><mi> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow></mrow></math> , its second electron gain enthalpy is:

options.text: Almost the same as that of the first
Negative, but less negative than the first
A more negative value than the first

solution.text:
Second electron gain enthalpy is always positive for every element because to overcome repulsion between an anion and electron,  energy has to be supplied.

O − + e − → O −2  ;  Δ H eg =+ve
